items.note: Association named, formed 1889, Gideon Vose first president, main creamery at Larrow Green 1891 (Story 1).
By-laws: paid by butterfat test not milk weight, station test determines pay (Story 1). Article VII not named; core rule present.
States the rule is what made the defect financially catastrophic (Story 1).
Effie Loomis, Wilbur Teague, Hobart Sill never named.
Section A has Selby as Gideon's son but gives no manager start year; elsewhere (B3, D3) the run asserts 1911, not 1913.
Station-gain ledger line not mentioned anywhere in Section A.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896 (Story 1). Borrowed Larrow Green glass not mentioned; core fact present.
Weigh, sample, test, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned (Story 1); bottle neck ruled for a full measure (Story 8).
Ammon & Sons at Tarnet, April 1897, in use 1 May 1897 (Story 2).
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 cc, 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93 (Story 2).
Never says the shortfall was flat, the same 0.19 in every month and every year. Gives a 0.19-0.21 range.
Nothing about pipettes being uncheckable without a burette, or no burette in the county.
Keddie 1861-1934, tester from the 1896 opening, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
His station book where he wrote down every figure is mentioned (Story 4). Thin, but the bolded element is present.
Section A gives 3.61 but never the 1896 average of 3.80. Both figures are required.
Nine weeks, 8 May-10 July 1911, borrowed measure, tests higher then back, question mark (Story 4). The 3.80 figure is missing but the core interval is right.
Section A calls Emmet his 'brother-in-law' but never names Orra Brant as Emmet's sister. Stated only in B2.
The 1919 circular is present, but not Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he cannot say why the figures are what they are.
Died 1934 under the imputation; records deposited at the Ordell County Historical Rooms.
Hessel Bottom wet ground, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest.
Brant's private weigh book from 1 Jan 1897 and the agreeing scales are not in Section A.
States the Hollow-vs-valley gap as 0.19-0.21 (Story 2; C1b, where Larrow Green is 3.78 against 3.61). This conflates the visible 0.17 with the true 0.19. The key says this loses the item.
Says the committee 'sampled herds in every season' rather than Jan-Mar 1908. The run also asserts the hay effect as partly true elsewhere.
Brant 1910 figures and the proportional loss (Vose Jerseys) not in Section A.
Weigh book passing to Roy Brant 1929 and lent to Ivy 1958 not in Section A.
Alder Corners Cheese Company never mentioned.
Four patrons hauling to Alder Corners from 1915 not mentioned.
Independence of the Alder Corners test not mentioned.
The 0.19 higher over sixteen seasons not mentioned.
Same milk tested differently in two buildings not mentioned.
Rosalie Cudd not mentioned.
Strawn named and independent, but no 1907-1936 span. The run dates his lactometer visits 'from 1908 forward' (Story 6).
Lactometer at every visit, never once found added water (Story 6).
Burette and condemnation of the whole lot are present, but Section A says only 'summer 1923'. 12 June is required.
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Has the 28 June and 2 July letters but gives the 1924 average as 3.85, not 3.80.
Crate in the loft since 1923 is present; the notebooks going to the college library in 1947 are missing. Both bolded elements are required.
Petition January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, two sittings in the station weigh room.
Three theories argued (water by the manager, theft by the tester, bog hay), none sustained by the board.
Four-book exhibit list and Strawn's 1923 notebook read for its other lines not in Section A (the list appears only in F).
Dismissed 30 April, before the finding; award 4 May 1925, $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
No one-fifth of $19,000 or link to the gain account; the run uses $19,600 as the loss.
Ivy Keddie b.1931, granddaughter, graduate student at State Agricultural College at Farland, under Leland Vaught.
Section A lists the records deposited, not that Ivy assembled records never before in one room (that framing is only in G).
February 1958 in the loft, but says eleven pipettes survived (NT-16), not nine.
No 95-percent reading, and not 3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood. Uses the 16.27 cascade.
Gives 67,000 lb and $19,600, with no ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him, twenty-four years after his death.
Granddaughter.
Ansel's son Duncan, whose daughter is Ivy. Great-niece is mentioned only as a corrected error.
Second cousins via Emmet/Orra siblings, Roy and Duncan first cousins.
Never raises full vs half siblings. Its 'left open' is about collaboration instead.
Gideon Vose.
No link to Gideon's Article VII making the test decisive, nor to the Vose Jerseys as the largest loser. Also asserts manager from 1911.
Asserts flatly 'There was no family relationship' (A01).
Treats the family denial as settling it, rather than saying no document names or denies a link.
True average 3.905, gap 0.30.
$19,600 and 19.4%, not $19,000 and one fifth.
120,000 lb, 8.3% / 7.7%; key 76,000, 5.00% of delivered / 5.26% of credited.
$77.93 with the line items.
72 pipettes right, but 1.33 cc short each; both required, key 0.88.
26 years and 21 full years 1902-1923, with a complaint-based reason; key 26 yr 6 wk and 25 full years 1898-1922.
A02: no declared indeterminacy. Offers ~1,100,000 lb (and names the first season as 1897), hedged as 'unreliable' oral tradition. Not treated as a definite assertion, so no -2.
Variable: the measure/pipette, borrowed 8 May-10 July.
Same tester, herds, pasture, season, machinery, acid, hand tester.
Only 'markedly higher' and 'fell back'; no 3.80 or 3.61.
Does not rule out all three rivals: its listed limits keep wet hay alive as a possible share of the gap.
Only two valid reasons (1911 interval, Strawn lactometer), both attributed to Falke; the third (family motive) is not on the key's list.
Argues independence and names the 1911 interval as holding without 1958.
A09 answered 'No.' as a verdict.
Yes, he knew the station tested low; cites the 1919 circular and the complaint renewed every decade.
Only two of the five: signed the ledger sheets, wrote the 1919 circular. Gives manager from 1911, and says nothing on the hearing or his never naming the glass.
No abstention; verdict 'He was looking for farmer misconduct or land problems, not manufacturing failure.'

Row 13 only (eleven vs nine families, resolved nine with a method). Its other items (opening-date confusion, 1911 duration, 12-28 June) are not keyed conflicts. Resolves the loss to 67,000/$19,600, which is wrong.
NT-18 (great-niece): names two carriers and breaks the tie by the family record and the corrective addendum. No other near-tie pairs.
A04, A06 and A10 not addressed as abstention conflicts.
Only self-contradiction offered is Oram's eleven/nine, which is not among the key's catalogued self-refutations and is already used for E-a. None of the listed ones is identified.
Uses 16.27 cc, 7.56%, 3.91 true, 3.85 after, and hay offsetting the error. No 95% or 0.19 = 5% of 3.80.
Watering (Selby Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer at every visit.
Theft defeated by the 1911 interval with the same tester.
Cites Bulletin 214 but then calls the hay theory 'partially correct', contributing 0.05. Half-adopted, not defeated.
A07 answered 'No.' as a verdict.
A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie suspected it was the glass.'
Summary is roughly 290 words despite its claimed 147.
Weigh book, station test book, inspector's notebooks, Association ledgers, arbitration documents.
16.27 cc and $19,600 as fact; wet hay 'partially true'.
Only 1897, 1958 and the two names. No one part in twenty (gives 16.27), no 76,000/$19,000 (gives $19,600), no explicit 1923.

Corruption: 1908 committee sampled 'in every season', i.e. the whole of 1908 (F096)
Corruption: bog hay thinned the cream, asserted as partly true (C1b, F1, F-expl 3, G) (F107)
Corruption: Strawn's lactometer visits/circuit from 1908 (Story 6, D2, F)
Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (B3, D3)
Corruption: a gap of 0.21 asserted ('the observed 0.21-point gap', F) (F076)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship denied flatly (B4)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper never questioned entries, 'No.' (D2)
Gullibility A03: verdict that the manager was not looking at the equipment (D3)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware, 'No.' (F)
Gullibility A05: tester believed it was the glass (F)
